title: Which part of CuteAFD's FP8 path shortens code reasoning: KDA FP8, FP8 head and FP8 prefill switched off cumulatively
question: On CuteAFD v4.0.0, which of the FP8 settings applied to the BF16-core checkpoint (KDA projections, vocabulary head, prefill activations) goes with its shorter code reasoning against the native 6-bit core?
engines: tpurtell/cuteafd v4.0.0 (coordinator image index sha256:e257bc61...), unmodified launcher
checkpoints: derived/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K4-Core-K6-BF16core @ 049c0180 (F arms; local derived checkpoint, not a producer release; built by results/2026-11-03-cuteafd-core-swap/prep/build_derived.py)
hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (300 W); GPU only, experts local

goals.headline: Identical in reasoning and content to the 2026-11-05 reply (60,617 reasoning characters each).

goals.question: Switching CuteAFD's FP8 settings off cumulatively on the BF16-core checkpoint, which step changes code reasoning length: KDA projections (F-kda / C-K6x), head (F-head / F-kda), prefill activations (F-pre / F-head)?

goals.headline: KDA step F-kda / C-K6x 1.31 [1.24, 1.38], detected (12 of 12 prompts); head step F-head / F-kda 1.02 [0.97, 1.07], not detected; prefill step F-pre / F-head 0.99 [0.97, 1.02], not detected (47 pairs). CuteAFD v4.0.0, BF16-core derived checkpoint; switching KDA FP8 off also turns off KDA output sharding on the two-GPU split, and the run does not separate the two.

goals.question: What are the switched-off settings in CuteAFD v4.0.0's design, and what reasons does the engine's author give for them?

design.instrument: reading of the tagged v4.0.0 source and docs

goals.status_note: The same design context was added to results/2026-11-06-vllm-code-thinking/CUTEAFD-FP8-PATH.md (VC-fp8-path-context).
goals.headline: The settings are the launcher's defaults: row128 FP8 KDA and FP8 head on both layouts; on the two-GPU head split, token-row KDA output ownership. The model notes and the option text describe BF16 KDA as the two-GPU default; the launcher comment and code select row128, which every launch logged. The cited author checks are teacher-forced on 512 positions.

goals.question: Where in the engine does the code-length difference arise: prefill or generation?

design.instrument: source reading (engine.rs line references) combined with this run's measurements

goals.headline: Judgement, not a measurement: most likely on the generation path (decode and speculative verify); prefill not excluded. Prompts are 1,155-1,758 tokens against medians of 50-68K reasoning tokens. Open: KDA in prefill vs generation; plain decode vs speculative verify; KDA format vs output sharding.

design.interval: 95% bootstrap over the 16 prompts (4,000, seed 20261108); Bonferroni intervals for 13 looks

goals.headline: Post hoc, 13 contrasts. 5 of 13 all-pass intervals exclude 0, all with the F arms or V-BF16 passing more often than C-K6/C-K6x (e.g. F-kda vs C-K6x +9.4 [+1.6, +18.8]); 2 after Bonferroni (F-pre vs C-K6x +17.5, Bonferroni [+4.8, +34.4]; F-pre vs C-K6 +15.9, [+3.2, +32.8]). C-K6 vs C-K6x +1.6 [-7.8, +10.9], not detected. F arms ran a day after the C arms; V arms are another engine; one prompt family.
